answer_1.quote: A summarization system that produces text summaries from transcripts can help, by providing users with great flexibility in navigating recordings, including but not limited to: meetings, interviews, podcasts, lectures, movies and TV series.

answer_2.quote: We use a variety of automatic evaluation metrics to assess the quality of transcript summaries. These metrics are broadly grouped into three categories: (a) traditional metrics comparing system and reference summaries based on lexical overlap, including ROUGE, ROUGEwe (w/ embeddings), BLEU and METEOR; (b) new metrics making use of contextualized embeddings to measure semantic similarity, e.g., BertScore and MoverScore; (c) question answering-based metrics...

answer_4.quote: We have worked with iMerit.net, a labor sourcing company, to recruit experienced evaluators from the U.S. and India to perform annotations. The workers are registered on Appen.com, a crowdsourcing platform, to complete the tasks and deliver results.
answer_4.guideline: The workers are asked to watch a video segment, typically 30 minutes or less, read the transcript, and then evaluate the quality of each system summary based on five criteria: informativeness, factuality, fluency, coherence, and redundancy.
